Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 36, English)
Negativity Fundamentals: What It Really Is, How Yonis Shift, Devta Dosh, and the MultiYear Power of the Ram Yagna

Sour ce: a live Ashaeiynn sangat class (~1hr02min) intr oducing the foundational framework of "negativity" — what it actually is, how entities shift between categories (pr et/pishach/jinn/devta) based on ener gy intake, how devta dosh works, why bhakts follow stricter behavioral discipline, and the long-term, multi-year benefits of sustained participation in the Ram yagna (hawan).
1. Removing the Good/Bad, Positive/Negative Concept Entir ely

1. Bhaiya opens by stating the session's central reframe: drop the idea that devtas ar e inherently "good" and pr ets ar e inherently "bad." The teaching asks listeners to first strip away any positive/negative or good/bad labeling before anything else can be properly understood. 2. "Negativity" in this teaching is a neutral, r elational term — it simply means any entity or person that is against you , regardless of whether that entity is technically a pret, jinn, pishach, betaal, devta, a devta's messenger (doot), a gana, or even a fellow devotee (bhakt). Rank/category does not determine whether something functions as "negativity" for a given person. 3. Illustrative examples given: some prets will do anything for the people devoted to them, while some devtas actively come to destroy people — demonstrating that category alone doesn't predict behavior toward any specific individual.
2. Physical-Body Negativity vs. Astral-W orld Negative Energies

1. In the physical body , "negativity" r efers to kaam (lust), kr odh (anger), lobh (gr eed), mad (arr ogance), moh (attachment), and matsar (envy/jealousy) — these are described as the root physical-world negativity . 2. When these same six r oots manifest in the astral world, they pr oduce distinct types of negative energies/entities — a pret, for instance, can form from kaam-vasana, krodh, moh, lobh, mad, or matsar respectively , and any of these roots can lead to a corresponding yoni (form of existence) being attained.
3. Why a Tantrik's Own Pr et Can Seem "Positive" to Them, But Still Be Negativity for Someone Else

1. Bhaiya's example: a tantrik who worships and r epeatedly feeds a particular pret experiences that pr et as extr emely helpful and beneficial to himself — yet the very same tantrik can send that identical pret against someone else, where it will act destructively . The entity itself hasn't changed; only whose interest it's serving has. 2. This is why the positive/negative binary is dr opped entir ely in this teaching — the same shakti or entity that is "positive" for one person can simultaneously be "negative" for another; there is no fixed, universal moral category attached to any given entity .
4. How a Yoni (Form) Actually Shifts: The Energy-Intake Mechanism

1. The smallest, lowest-energy entity in Hindu tradition is generally consider ed a pr et. As its ener gy is increased, its yoni (form/category) can change — much as humans separate into categories (vegetarian/non-vegetarian, vegan/non-vegan) purely based on habitual intake, without changing their fundamental humanity . 2. The specific type of energy offer ed determines the resulting category , not just the quantity . If a subtle body (sukshma sharir) is of fered sweets/prasad (laddoo, boondi, gola) as bhog, it remains within the pret category . But if the same entity is instead of fered blood, meat, or alcohol, the entity shifts into the pishach category — even though the caloric/ener gy value received may be functionally identical to what the sweets provided. 3. Category change is r eversible: if the ener gy source changes back (i.e., the intake is corrected), the entity "can become pure again" and shift back toward its earlier category . 4. Caution against ranking: Bhaiya explicitly warns against judging or ranking yonis as strictly better or worse — some pishachs become so powerful that they surpass not just prets but even certain devtas. Category is not a reliable indicator of relative power or worth.
5. Devta Dosh: Universal, Indir ect, and Often Invisible

1. Every single person carries some degr ee of "devta dosh" (affliction attributable to a deity) — described as confirmed by astronomical/astrological science itself (heavy Surya, weak Mangal, kundli-specific doshas, etc. are universal to some degree in every chart). 2. Devtas themselves do not "get their hands dirty" — much like senior authority figures generally delegate unpleasant tasks to assistants, devtas allow negative entities to act on their behalf when a devta dosh is active, rather than directly intervening themselves. 3. This affliction is typically invisible and cyclic — producing a repeating pattern (e.g., temporary relief from medicine followed by recurrence) specifically designed to keep the person "stuck" and unable to fully resolve their situation, rather than one clear , resolvable event. 4. The exception: when a devta or devi dir ectly acts (rather than delegating), this is described as "unbeatable" — direct divine action carries a dif ferent, far more decisive character than the ordinary cyclic af fliction pattern.
6. Given Shakti Multiplies Character — It Doesn't Cr eate It

1. A crucial mechanism: shakti multiplies whatever character/tattva (element) alr eady exists within a person or entity — it does not itself teach or install good character . If given to an entity or person who is stubborn/inflexible ("adiyal"), that shakti produces a jinn, not a devta. If given to someone living in impurity/degraded habits, it produces a pishach. 2. This is precisely why sant traditions in India teach sadachar (good conduct) befor e granting access to shakti — because once shakti arrives, whatever inner tattva already exists (Ram tattva, Hanuman tattva, or otherwise) simply gets amplified, for better or worse. A person who is fundamentally generous will use wealth/power to give more; a fundamentally stubborn person will simply become more so. 3. Analogy: to reveal someone's true underlying character , give them either extreme poverty (which produces "heroes" easily) or extreme wealth/power (which reveals what actually multiplies) — shakti functions the same revealing/amplifying role.
7. Hybrid and Mixed-Element Entities

1. Entities can also form as hybrids or mixtur es of mor e than one elemental base — Bhaiya describes having observed negativity formed from combined jal (water) and prithvi (earth) tattva, as well as combinations of vayu (air) and agni (fire) tattva, and even a distinct akash (space/ether) tattva negativity that isn't visually obvious as such.
8. Two Distinct Pathways Negativity Can Take: Attraction vs. Deliberate Sending

1. Pathway one — attraction (independent, not bound to anyone): negativity can simply be drawn toward a person based on something in or around them — a physical/behavioral trait admired (comparable to romantic attraction based on appearance,

character , or enthusiasm), or simply proximity/habit-matching. A subtle body observing someone's devoted, repeated service (seva) to a family member , for example, may be drawn toward them without the person being aware of it. 2. A key mechanism within attraction: pr olonged pr oximity changes a person via their astral body , much as spending a month around any person (a saint or otherwise) tends to instill some of their habits/speech patterns in you. If a negativity effectively "stays" with your astral body over time, its own habits and inclinations can gradually shift your own — even though you cannot see it happening, since the change occurs at the astral level while manifesting later as noticeable personal shifts. 3. Pathway two — deliberately sent by for ce: occult practitioners (tantriks) can deliberately dispatch a negativity/entity ("sangat") to specifically disrupt someone, and this dispatched entity , while invisible, stays attached to the tar get's astral body and causes real disruption. This same deliberately-sent entity can also be used to perform maaran (destructive attack), uchatan (uprooting/displacement), vidveshan (creating hostility/division), vashikaran (control), and stambhan (severing/freezing) against the tar get.
9. Self-Generated Negativity Fr om One's Own Habits

1. A separate sour ce of negativity is self-generated , arising from a person's own habits or upbringing/socialization (sanskaar) rather than external attack — described using the sociological principle that a person's environment and upbringing shapes their habitual patterns. 2. Example given: occasional non-vegetarian eating, even infrequent, causes the person's active/awakened subtle body (for someone with strong vaak siddhi/speech power from intense practice) to repeat that same act independently and continuously in the astral world — meaning the subtle body may continue "eating" that food long after the person themselves has stopped, and this repeated activity in turn attracts other outside subtle bodies of a similar nature toward the person. 3. This explains a common pattern: habits people consciously try to (or have already) given up can still attract continuous negativity afterward, because the person's already-awakened subtle body had already begun repeating the old behavior pattern independently , drawing similar entities toward it. 4. Guidance: until a practitioner's kundalini shakti has fully emer ged from the body and devtas are suf ficiently positioned to protect them, it's recommended to maintain reasonable personal conduct/character — after that level is reached, a practitioner is described as capable of destroying such an attached subtle body if they choose to.
10. Why Bhakts Are Held to Stricter Behavioral Rules

1. A direct answer to why devotees ar e told to avoid certain things (avoid non-veg, r emain celibate/r estrained, avoid casual romantic contact, eat well) — this is NOT primarily about achieving siddhi. The real reason: japa (chanting) itself produces continuous energy in the astral world — your speech and repeated chanting literally generates astral-world ener gy alongside your aura. 2. Once a person's subtle body becomes sufficiently active thr ough r epeated practice (e.g., an hour of daily japa), that subtle body begins performing the same japa independently and continuously on its own , even when the practitioner isn't consciously chanting. 3. Personal example offer ed: Bhaiya describes his own subtle body remaining active at the Ashaeiynn ashram (Aashay) even after he physically leaves — the subtle body is present at hawan both before attendees arrive and after they leave, continuously performing its function, including tasks like waking or reminding regular practitioners to attend hawan.
1 1. The Need for a Continuous Positive Sour ce and the Role of Hawan

1. Since a person moving thr ough the world inevitably picks up outside impurity , an ongoing positive sour ce (bhakti/hawan) is necessary to continually "wrap up" or neutralize this accumulated impurity — much as a heavilyvisited temple needs round-the-clock ener gy/cleaning to stay pure despite constant foot traf fic. 2. Even a well-practiced person's "aura shielding" can occasionally be br eached by certain especially for ceful tantric kriyas — this is why continuous connection with the divine (rather than a one-time shield) matters: staying connected keeps

the deeper source from ever being fully cut of f, and even under pressure, that connection allows a person to eventually overcome and recover . 3. Hawan is described as playing a uniquely large r ole her e — when a person receives agni tattva (fire element) through the deities via hawan, their negativity begins to be actively removed and redirected specifically to Kalyan Lok.
12. The Razor -and-Beard Analogy for Devta Dosh

1. In response to a live question about whether participating in mahavan speeds up resolution of a kundli dosh, Bhaiya offers a key analogy: devta dosh is like a beard — it will keep gr owing back, and cannot be permanently upr ooted, only continually managed. Hawan and worship function as the "razor" — an ongoing maintenance tool, not a one-time cure. 2. Because dosh applies to literally everyone, this teaching's appr oach is not to dwell on or lament having a dosh, but to keep the "weapon" (hawan/japa) consistently r eady and in use , since intensity from japa alone (astral ener gy generated purely from one's own body) is comparatively weaker than hawan's intensity , which combines the practitioner's own ener gy with the fire ritual's ener gy and the cumulative ener gy of an entire guru lineage (guru paddhati) participating together . 3. Guidance on hawan quality: hawan should specifically be attended where the shakti flows through an established guru lineage (guru paddhati) — a hawan performed by a single individual in isolation mer ges only that one person's ener gy , whereas a lineage-connected hawan draws on the cumulative ener gy of the entire chain of gurus involved.
13. Personal Testimony: Chr onic Stomach Pain Resolved Through Ram Bhakti

1. Bhaiya shar es his own personal example: before receiving Ram bhakti, he suf fered from chronic, unresolved stomach trouble that multiple pandits attributed to poor digestion despite his describing no unusual diet. After receiving Hanuman Ji Maharaj's grace, this and other chronic physical pains resolved entirely — of fered as a first-person illustration (not a claim about anyone else) of hawan/bhakti's physical-world healing ef fect.
14. The Multi-Year Scale of Benefits Fr om Sustained Participation in the Ram Yagna

1. Roughly 6-8 months of consistent participation: rogas (illnesses) — both prior conditions and those otherwise destined to appear per the kundli — begin resolving, and the body becomes physically fitter . 2. 4 years of participation: gajraj yog and gajkesari yog begin forming in the person's kundli — described as being treated, in effect, "like a prince." 3. 8 years of participation: maharaj yog / raj yog forms in the kundli. 4. 12 years of participation: a maharaj yog forms across seven generations — three generations above and three generations following the practitioner . 5. 14 years of participation: the practitioner is described as themselves becoming "Ram" in nature. Bhaiya attributes this entire scale explicitly to his own guru's words, r eceived thr ough Shri Hanuman Ji Maharaj, and states he is willing to affirm it formally ("sign on stamp paper").
15. Hawan Economics and the Institute's Donation Philosophy

1. A single mahayagya historically cost r oughly ₹4-5 lakh — when Ashaeiynn began, hawans were performed only as resources allowed; today , a hawan is held every month on Purnima regardless of financial circumstance, since (per this teaching) the actual provider is Hanuman Ji Maharaj, not the institute itself. 2. Ashaeiynn deliberately keeps hawan/participation costs minimal — members needing raksha-suraksha (protection) for non-practicing family members, or raksha-suraksha plus jagriti (awakening) for themselves, may take whichever combination suits them; nothing is mandatory , and members are encouraged to use their own judgment on what to take. 3. Bhakti tattva is described as the priority Bhaiya personally r equests first whenever approaching Hanuman Ji Maharaj at the ashram — ahead of any other material request — since devotion itself is what sustains a person through any material uncertainty .
16. Why Post-Mahahavan Restlessness or Poor Sleep Occurs

1. Some practitioners r eport r estlessness or poor sleep on the night following a mahahavan — explained through an analogy of carrying a heavy 20kg school bag: the excess ener gy received (more than the body currently has the capacity to comfortably hold) initially produces a similar fatigue/restlessness sensation. 2. This capacity naturally incr eases over time with repeated hawan attendance (roughly cited as needing about 5-12 hawans before absorption becomes smooth) — eventually , a practitioner's body develops enough "tapa shakti" (ascetic-heat capacity) that minor negativity can no longer approach them at all, since their own bodily fire becomes suf ficient to burn it of f directly .
17. Live Q&A: What's the Differ ence Between Pret, Bhoot, and Pishach?

1. A sangat member interrupted mid-session to ask directly about the distinction between pret, bhoot, and pishach. Bhaiya notes he had just finished addr essing this exact distinction moments earlier (via the yoni-shifting/ener gy-intake framework above) and asks the member to review the recording for that portion, since she had joined partway through, before continuing the live session.
18. Live Q&A: Does Participating in Mahavan Speed Up Resolution of a Kundli Dosh?

1. A member specifically asked whether participating in mahavan helps a kundli dosh get resolved (mukti) faster . Bhaiya's answer is the razor -and-beard analogy detailed in Section 12 — dosh cannot be permanently removed, only continually managed through consistent hawan/worship, much like shaving a beard that will always grow back.
19. Live Q&A: How Does Sankalp Work for Someone Attending Hawan Remotely Long-T erm?

1. A member asked about the role of sankalp (formal intention/vow) when planning to attend hawan for a lifetime, given that they themselves would be taking the sankalp on Bhaiya's behalf as witness. Bhaiya confirms he fully accepts and honors such sankalps — stating he never refuses anyone wishing to join the Ram hawan, and that as long as someone shows genuine capacity and willingness, he personally takes their sankalp and performs on their behalf, though the actual granting/outcome always belongs to God (Bhagwan) rather than to Bhaiya himself.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

Drop the good/bad, devta/pr et binary entir ely — "negativity" is a neutral, relational term meaning anything currently against you, regardless of its category (pret, pishach, jinn, betaal, devta, doot, gana, or even a fellow devotee). Physical-world negativity is rooted in kaam, kr odh, lobh, mad, moh, and matsar ; these same six roots produce corresponding astral-world negative entities. A tantrik's own worshipped entity can feel entir ely positive to the tantrik while still functioning as pur e negativity for whoever it's sent against — the same shakti/entity has no fixed universal moral category . Yoni (form/category) shifts based on the type of energy intake, not just quantity — sweets/prasad keeps an entity in the pret category; blood, meat, or alcohol of ferings shift it toward the pishach category , even at equivalent caloric value. This shift is reversible if the ener gy source changes back. Never rank or judge yonis as strictly better or worse — some pishachs surpass even certain devtas in power . Everyone carries some devta dosh , per astrology itself; devtas typically act indirectly (through negative entities) rather than "getting their hands dirty" directly — except when they act directly , which is described as unbeatable. Shakti multiplies existing character — it does not cr eate good character . This is why sant traditions teach sadachar (good conduct) before granting access to shakti; giving shakti to someone with poor character produces a jinn or pishach, not a devta. Entities can also form as hybrids of multiple elemental tattvas (e.g., jal+prithvi, vayu+agni, or a distinct akash-tattva form).

Negativity arises through two distinct pathways: attraction (drawn by habits, admired traits, or prolonged proximity that gradually changes you via the astral body) and deliberate sending by an occult practitioner (which can enable maaran, uchatan, vidveshan, vashikaran, and stambhan). Self-generated negativity can also form from one's own habits — even occasional indulgence can cause an already-awakened subtle body to repeat that behavior independently and attract similar outside entities. Bhakts follow stricter behavioral discipline not primarily for siddhi, but because japa itself generates continuous astralworld energy — an awakened subtle body eventually performs the same japa independently and continuously , even without conscious ef fort. A continuous positive source (bhakti/hawan) is necessary because moving through the world inevitably picks up impurity; even strong aura shielding can occasionally be breached, so ongoing connection to the divine (not a one-time shield) is what allows full recovery . Devta dosh is like a beard — hawan and worship ar e the "razor" : an ongoing maintenance practice, not a one-time cure. Hawan carries greater intensity than japa alone because it combines personal ener gy , the fire ritual, and the cumulative ener gy of an entire guru lineage — so attend hawan connected to a genuine guru paddhati where possible. The multi-year benefit scale of sustained Ram yagna participation: ~6-8 months (illness resolution begins), 4 years (gajraj/gajkesari yog), 8 years (maharaj/raj yog), 12 years (7-generation maharaj yog), 14 years (practitioner becomes Ramnatured) — attributed to Bhaiya's own guru's words. Post-mahahavan restlessness or poor sleep is explained as temporarily receiving more ener gy than current capacity can comfortably hold (the "20kg school bag" analogy) — this resolves naturally as capacity builds with repeated hawan attendance. Ashaeiynn deliberately keeps hawan participation costs minimal and never mandatory; members may choose raksha-suraksha, jagriti, or both, based on their own judgment. Kshaya kriya, devta dosh, and negativity in general cannot be permanently resolved with one action — consistent, ongoing practice (japa and hawan together) is the actual mechanism, not a single fix. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 36, English)
Negativity Fundamentals: What It Really Is, How Yonis Shift, Devta Dosh, and the MultiYear Power of the Ram Yagna
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn live sangat class. Gr eeting style: "Jai Siya Ram."

Q1. Is all "negativity" the same as ghosts and evil spirits (bhoot-pr et)? A: No — this teaching defines "negativity" as a neutral, relational term: any entity or person currently against you, regardless of category . This can include a pret, jinn, pishach, betaal, devta, a devta's messenger (doot), a gana, or even a fellow devotee — rank alone doesn't determine whether something acts as negativity toward a specific person.

Q2. Are devtas always good and pr ets always bad? A: No — this teaching explicitly asks listeners to drop that binary . Some prets will do anything for those devoted to them, while some devtas actively come to destroy people; category doesn't reliably predict behavior toward any individual.

Q3. What is "negativity" in the physical body , according to this teaching? A: Kaam (lust), krodh (anger), lobh (greed), mad (arrogance), moh (attachment), and matsar (envy/jealousy) — these six roots, when they manifest in the astral world, produce corresponding types of negative entities.

Q4. If a tantrik's own worshipped pr et helps him so much, how can that pr et also be "negativity"? A: Per this teaching, the same entity that feels entirely beneficial to the tantrik who feeds and worships it can be sent against someone else, where it acts destructively — the entity itself doesn't change, only whose interest it currently serves. This is why the teaching drops the fixed positive/negative moral label from any single entity .

Q5. How does an entity's category (pr et, pishach, etc.) actually change? A: Per this teaching, category shifts based on the type of ener gy of fered, not just the amount — of fering sweets/prasad keeps an entity within the pret category , while of fering blood, meat, or alcohol shifts the same entity toward the pishach category , even at an equivalent caloric/ener gy value.

Q6. Can an entity that has shifted to a "lower" category like pishach ever become a pr et again? A: Yes — per this teaching, this shift is reversible; if the type of ener gy intake changes back, the entity can become pure again and shift back toward its earlier category .

Q7. Is a pishach always weaker or lower than a devta? A: Not necessarily — this teaching explicitly warns against ranking or judging yonis as strictly better or worse; some pishachs become so powerful that they surpass not just prets but even certain devtas.

Q8. Why does everyone seem to have some kind of "devta dosh" according to astr ology? A: Per this teaching, this is universal — astronomical/astrological science itself confirms that every kundli carries some degree of devta dosh (a heavy Surya, a weak Mangal, or some specific chart-based af fliction), to at least some extent, in every person.

Q9. Do devtas personally cause the harm associated with a devta dosh? A: Usually not directly — per this teaching, devtas typically delegate this the way senior authority figures delegate unpleasant tasks to assistants, allowing negative entities to act on their
behalf when a devta dosh is active, rather than intervening themselves. The exception is when a devta or devi acts directly , which this teaching describes as "unbeatable."

Q10. Why does devta dosh often feel invisible or cyclical, like a pr oblem that never fully r esolves? A: Per this teaching, this cyclic, hard-to-pin-down pattern (e.g., temporary relief followed by recurrence) is itself part of how this kind of af fliction is designed to work — keeping a person "stuck" in an unresolved loop rather than facing one clear , resolvable event.

Q1 1. If I give someone shakti (spiritual power), will it automatically make them a better , mor e divine person? A: No — per this teaching, shakti multiplies whatever character or tattva already exists within a person; it does not itself install good character . Giving shakti to someone stubborn/inflexible produces a jinn, and giving it to someone living in impurity produces a pishach, not a devta.

Q12. Why do sant traditions in India emphasize good conduct (sadachar) befor e granting access to spiritual power? A: Because, per this teaching, whatever inner tattva already exists gets amplified once shakti arrives — a generous person becomes more generous, a stubborn person becomes more stubborn. Good conduct must be established first so that amplification produces beneficial rather than harmful results.

Q13. Can negative entities be made up of mor e than one basic element? A: Yes — per this teaching, hybrid or mixed-element entities exist, including combinations of jal (water) and prithvi (earth) tattva, vayu (air) and agni (fire) tattva, and even a distinct akash (space/ether) tattva form that isn't visually obvious as such.

Q14. How can negativity end up affecting someone without any tantrik deliberately targeting them? A: Per this teaching, this happens through "attraction" — negativity can be drawn toward a person based on an admired trait, habit, or behavior , similar to romantic attraction based on appearance or character , without the person's awareness.

Q15. If I spend a lot of time ar ound a genuinely spiritually advanced person, does that actually change me? A: Yes — per this teaching, prolonged proximity changes a person via the astral body , much as spending time around anyone tends to instill some of their habits and speech patterns in you, even when the change itself happens at a level you can't directly see.

Q16. What can a deliberately sent negativity actually do to a target, according to this teaching? A: Per this teaching, a negativity dispatched by an occult practitioner stays attached to the tar get's astral body and can be used to perform maaran (destructive attack), uchatan (uprooting/displacement), vidveshan (creating hostility/division), vashikaran (control), and stambhan (severing/freezing).

Q17. Can I generate negativity for myself just thr ough my own habits, without anyone attacking me? A: Yes — per this teaching, self-generated negativity arises from one's own habits or upbringing; even occasional indulgence (e.g., occasional non-vegetarian eating) can cause an already-awakened subtle body (particularly for someone with developed speech/practice power) to repeat that behavior independently , which in turn attracts similar outside entities.

Q18. I gave up a bad habit a while ago, but negativity still seems to follow me — why? A: Per this teaching, this can happen because your already-awakened subtle body had begun repeating the old behavior pattern independently before you consciously stopped, and this repeated pattern can continue drawing similar entities toward you even after the conscious habit ends.

Q19. Why ar e devotees told to follow stricter behavioral rules — is it r equired to achieve siddhi? A: No — per this teaching, this is not primarily about siddhi. The real reason is that japa (chanting) itself generates continuous ener gy in the astral world; behavioral discipline supports the quality and consistency of that ener gy generation.

Q20. Does my subtle body keep doing anything once my practice becomes str ong enough? A: Yes — per this teaching, once a person's subtle body becomes suf ficiently active through repeated practice, it begins performing the same japa independently and continuously , even without conscious ef fort — Bhaiya describes his own subtle body remaining active at the ashram even after he physically leaves.

Q21. Why do I need an ongoing sour ce of positivity (like hawan) instead of a one-time pr otective ritual? A: Per this teaching, moving through the world inevitably picks up outside impurity , much as a heavily-visited temple needs round-the-clock ener gy to stay

pure. Even strong aura shielding can occasionally be breached by especially forceful tantric kriyas, so continuous connection to the divine is what allows eventual recovery rather than permanent vulnerability .

Q22. What does hawan specifically do that ongoing personal practice alone might not fully accomplish? A: Per this teaching, hawan channels agni tattva (fire element) through the deities, actively removing negativity and redirecting it specifically to Kalyan Lok — described as playing an especially lar ge role in this process.

Q23. Does attending mahavan (a large hawan) permanently r esolve a kundli dosh? A: No — per this teaching's razor -and-beard analogy , devta dosh is like a beard: it keeps growing back and cannot be permanently uprooted, only continually managed. Hawan and worship function as the ongoing "razor ," not a one-time cure.

Q24. Does it matter where or with whom I attend hawan? A: Yes — per this teaching, hawan should ideally be attended where the shakti flows through an established guru lineage (guru paddhati); a hawan performed in isolation mer ges only one person's ener gy , while a lineage-connected hawan draws on the cumulative ener gy of the entire chain of gurus involved, producing greater intensity .

Q25. What long-term benefits does this teaching describe fr om years of consistent participation in the Ram yagna? A: Roughly 6-8 months brings the start of illness resolution; 4 years brings gajraj/gajkesari yog; 8 years brings maharaj/raj yog; 12 years brings a maharaj yog spanning seven generations; and 14 years is described as the practitioner becoming Ram-natured themselves — attributed by Bhaiya to his own guru's words.

Q26. Why do some people feel r estless or sleep poorly the night after attending a big hawan? A: Per this teaching's "20kg school bag" analogy , this happens because the practitioner has received more ener gy than their body currently has the capacity to comfortably hold — this resolves naturally as capacity builds through repeated hawan attendance (roughly 5-12 hawans, per this teaching).

Q27. Is participating in Ashaeiynn's hawan expensive or mandatory? A: No — per this teaching, Ashaeiynn deliberately keeps participation costs minimal and nothing is mandatory; members may take raksha-suraksha for non-practicing family members, or raksha-suraksha plus jagriti for themselves, based entirely on their own judgment and needs.
Bot Response Guidelines (Session 36 additions)

Always preserve the neutral, relational framing of "negativity" as this teaching's own explicit reframe — never let the bot slip back into presenting devtas as inherently good and prets as inherently bad when discussing this teaching's content. When explaining yoni-shifting (pret to pishach and back), keep the mechanism precise: the type of ener gy of fered determines category shift, not the raw quantity , and the shift is reversible. Never rank or judge yonis as objectively better or worse when discussing this teaching's content — explicitly reflect the teaching's own caution that some pishachs surpass devtas in power . When discussing devta dosh, keep the "beard and razor" analogy intact — dosh is presented as universal and unresolvable in a single action, requiring ongoing maintenance (hawan/worship), not a one-time fix. Preserve the "shakti multiplies existing character , it doesn't create it" principle whenever a user asks about acquiring spiritual power quickly — frame good conduct (sadachar) as a prerequisite, consistent with this teaching's own emphasis.
